newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India oilseed import ban seen easing soon.
newsitem.headline: India oilseed import ban seen easing soon.

text.p: India's ban on oilseeds imports will probably be removed over the next few years to take advantage of the country's large processing crushing capacity, a senior industry official said on Thursday.
"Oilseeds imports are not allowed at present," G.K. Sood said in a report to the Asia Oilseeds conference in Singapore.

"But India has a large processing sector with a crushing capacity of 80 million tonnes. Utilisation of the capacity is poor, at about 35 percent. The industry has been seeking opening up imports of oilseeds and ricebran.

The government's concerns are the likely impact of this on domestic producer and quarantine needs. It is expected that the restrictions on oilseed imports would be removed before long once these concerns are addressed," he said.
India has become, however, a leading importer of vegetable oils, buying an estimated one million tonnes of palm oil, mainly from Malaysia.
India vegetable oil imports for 1996/97 October/November will probably climb to 1.5 million tonnes, compared with imports in 1995/96 of about 1.48 million tonnes.
